theater: 淮河中游硤石（今安徽鳳陽）

battle.name: 硤石之戰
battle.theater: 淮河中游硤石（今安徽鳳陽）
battle.brief: 西周宣王十一年（約前514年），徐偃王率徐國與淮夷聯兵西進，周宣王調王師與諸侯之師東出，會戰於淮河中游的硤石。周軍以車兵為骨幹，步兵與弓箭手壓上，徐軍依淮水與崗地抵抗，一戰崩潰，徐偃王退保淮東。此役後淮夷北遷，徐國失去屏障。卡面埃及長矛並非戰場所用，卻是同類長柄刺擊兵的祖型。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 硤石之戰是西周王室聯軍與徐國—淮夷聯軍在淮河中游的一次會戰。周一方由三支力量拼成：周王直屬的「王師」，即《詩經·大雅·常武》所說的六師；受命出征的諸侯之師；以及隨軍的王朝卿士與各國帥師。六師是西周常備軍，平時駐鎬京與成周一帶，戰時才沿汝水、淮水諸道東南行；諸侯之師由各國卿大夫率領，甲兵、車乘與糧秣多自備，因此聯軍的集結與展開都受各國距離與糧道制約。西周的「師」是基本編制單位，按傳世文獻的追述，三軍（中軍與左右師）合七千五百人、六師合一萬五千人，但這組數字出自晚出的制度追述，只能當作編制規模的參照，不是硤石戰場上的實點人數；沒有任何一次西周會戰留下可靠的雙方兵員帳目。徐一方則是兩個鬆散部分的臨時聯盟：江淮大國徐國，以及沿淮水下游與淮南居住、彼此並無統一首領的淮夷諸部。徐國君主徐偃王居淮水中下游的都邑（後世稱徐州、徐城，在今江蘇泗洪、安徽泗縣一帶），控扼淮河與泗、汴水交會處，是周室南下江淮的門戶；淮夷則以舟楫為長，沿淮水活動，能順流直下，卻缺少可以統轄大軍的常設編制。雙方合併的關鍵是徐偃王的權威：他以東方諸國之首的身份號召淮夷，淮夷則以人數與舟船補充徐國所缺的兵力和水戰之力。指揮系統方面，周方以周王總攬，誓師、列陣與戰機決斷都在王本人與卿士手中，卿士中最可能隨軍的是《常武》詩中出現的召穆公虎；徐方則以徐偃王為最高首領，淮夷各部由自己的首領帶領，戰前靠使者往還與盟誓維繫，戰中容易各行其是。
countriesEn: The battle of Xiashi was a meeting of arms on the middle Huai between a coalition of the Western Zhou royal house and a coalition of the state of Xu together with the Huai barbarians. The Zhou side was put together out of three elements: the royal host itself, the six divisions of the Shujing's Great Odes in the Great Odes chapter Changwu calls them; the contingents of the feudal lords sent to the campaign; and the court ministers of the dynasty and the commanders of the various states who marched with them. The six divisions were the standing army of the Western Zhou, normally stationed around Haojing and Chengzhou, and they moved only when war came, along the roads that ran by the Ru and the Huai; the feudal contingents were led by the great officers of their own states and brought their own armour, their own war chariots and largely their own grain, so that the mustering and the deployment of the coalition were governed by the distances and the supply lines of each state. The division was the basic unit of Zhou military organisation, and the transmitted description of the system gives three armies, the central host with the right and the left, at two thousand five hundred men apiece, and six divisions at fifteen thousand in all; but those figures come from a late systematisation and can serve only as a scale for the organisation, not as a headcount on the field at Xiashi, and no Western Zhou battle has left a reliable muster for both sides. The Xu side was a temporary alliance of two loose parts: the great state of Xu in the middle and lower Huai valley, and the several Huai barbarian groups who lived along the lower river and south of it, none of whom had a single commander. The ruler of Xu, King Xuan of Xu, held his capital in the middle-lower Huai valley, the place later called Xuzhou or the City of Xu, in the neighbourhood of present-day Sihong in Jiangsu and Sixian in Anhui, where the Huai meets the Si and the Bian; that position commands the gateway by which the Zhou court reached the river country. The Huai barbarians were at home on the water, moving along the river and able to drift downstream in force, but they had no standing organisation capable of holding an army together. What held the two together was the authority of King Xuan of Xu: he called the Huai groups as the leading ruler of the eastern states, and they supplied him with the numbers and the boats his own state lacked. On the Zhou side command was in the king's hands, and the oath, the deployment and the decision on the moment of battle rested with the king and his ministers, of whom the likeliest to be in the field is Xiao Mu, Duke of Shao, who appears in the poem Changwu. On the Xu side King Xuan of Xu was the supreme commander and each Huai group was led by its own chief; the alliance was held together before the battle by messengers and oaths, and in the battle it was easy for the parts to act each for itself.
people: 留下姓名的多數屬於勝方。周宣王姬靜是這場戰爭的總帥：他調六師、會諸侯之師、親自誓師並在陣前指揮，成敗由他一身承擔。宣王在位時曾兩度用兵於東南與西陲，時人把他這段統治稱為「宣王中興」，而硤石之役正是「中興」敘事中最被反覆引用的戰役之一。召穆公虎是他手下最能打的卿士之一，《詩經·大雅·常武》即以召穆公為作詩主體，詩中記宣王對徐戎用兵、淮夷臣服、申伯受封與築謝城安置等事，因此召穆公是這場戰役最可能身在其列的統帥級人物；若此役繫於《常武》所寫的那次用兵，召穆公很可能就是實際前線統軍者。申伯是戰後被推到南方的諸侯，《常武》記「王命召伯，徹申伯土田」，即由召伯整飭申伯的田地、築城安置，用以屏蔽淮北，是周室安置淮夷、經營南土的關鍵一環。徐方唯一留下名字的是徐偃王；傳說他的「偃」字是為避某位楚王的名諱而改，此說出自後世雜書，可信度有限，但徐國君主確實以「偃王」見稱，說明這位君主在傳統記憶中突出到連名字都被附會。淮夷各部首領的名字沒有進入正史，只在金文與詩篇中以「淮夷」整體出現。還有兩件不能當人物、卻等同於人物存在的東西：其一是被派往淮夷戰線的周將兮甲，也就是虢季子白，兮甲盤銘文記他隨王伐獫狁、戰淮夷，並記王錫他馬四匹與車，這位重臣很可能就在這條戰線上；其二是師旂，師旂鼎銘文記他經手淮夷所獻的弓矢與俘獲，同樣是一位在淮夷戰線上留下名字的人。
peopleEn: Those whose names survive belong for the most part to the winning side. King Xuan of Zhou, Ji Jing, was the commander in chief of this war: he called out the six divisions, mustered the contingents of the feudal lords, swore the army in himself and led it in person, so that the outcome of the campaign was carried on his own shoulders. King Xuan fought in the southeast and on the western frontier more than once, and his contemporaries called that stretch of his reign the revival of King Xuan, and the battle of Xiashi is among the most frequently cited of the campaigns that stand behind that claim. Duke Shao Mu, whose personal name was Hu, was one of the ablest of his ministers, and the Shujing's Great Odes chapter Changwu is written from his point of view: the poem records the king's war against the Xu Rong, the submission of the Huai barbarians, the enfeoffment of the Shen Bo and the building of the city of Xie to settle them, and so Duke Shao Mu is the most likely of the commanders to have been present. If this battle is identified with the campaign the poem describes, then Duke Shao Mu was very probably the man who led the advance in the field. The Shen Bo was a lord who was pushed forward into the south after the war; the Changwu records that the king ordered Duke Shao to straighten out the Shen Bo's fields, to survey and to settle him, so as to hold the north bank of the Huai, and this was the key step by which the Zhou court resettled the Huai barbarians and managed the southern frontier. The only name on the Xu side is King Xuan of Xu. The story that his character Yanyan was changed to avoid the personal name of a king of Chu comes from later miscellaneous writings and cannot be much trusted; but the ruler of Xu is indeed known as King Xuan, which shows that he stood out in the traditional memory so sharply that even his name acquired a legend. The names of the chiefs of the Huai groups never entered the standard histories and appear only in bronze inscriptions and in poems, as the collective term Huaiyi. Two further things cannot be called people yet are equivalent to them: first, the Zhou commander sent to the Huai front, Xi Jia, also known as the Ji of the Zhai clan, whose pan inscription records that he followed the king against the Xianyun and fought the Huaiyi, and that the king granted him four horses and a chariot, so that this heavy minister may well have stood on that very front; second, Shi Qi, whose ding inscription records his handling of bows and arrows surrendered by the Huaiyi and of the prisoners taken, likewise a man who left a name on the Huaiyi front.
kits: 先說清楚一件容易被誤讀的事：卡面上這把埃及長矛（Egyptian spear，前3200年）並沒有隨周軍出現在硤石。它是埃及早王朝的典型刺擊兵器，銅或青銅矛頭作柳葉形，有中脊與兩側刃，用皮繩或木楔綁在木桿上；那爾梅調色板背面的戰爭場面、蝎子權杖頭與象形骨標籤上的獵象圖，都留下當時人持矛、持斧、持弓的樣子。它的功能定位很清楚：雙手持握的中距刺擊，必要時也可脫手投擲，配以木胎蒙革的盾，與後來讓位給斧、鎬的分工互補。放到硤石之役的裝備表裡，它對應的正是周軍陣上成排的矛。西周的矛以青銅矛頭為主，形制為柳葉形，中起脊脊，兩側開刃，後接圓管狀的鐏或鏃，插在木桿上再以皮繩纏紮，桿身常見皮條或竹篾纏束，柄端有時再加銅箍；河南三門峽上村嶺西周墓地、河南浚縣辛村衛國墓地等處出土的成組青銅戈矛，就是這一時期兵器的實物樣本，辛村的車馬坑更顯示當時車兵怎樣配置：雙輪單軸，一車四馬，車上三人，一御者、一持戈者、一執矛或弓者。與矛並列的是戈，戈援有鋒、內出銎，裝在柲上作鉤啄與斫擊之用，這是西周步兵與車兵的另一支骨幹；弓以竹木為身，箭鏃有石、骨、青銅三等，用來在接戰前壓制對手與騷擾兩翼；防護以皮甲、革胄與木盾為主，金屬甲胄在西周仍罕見。淮夷一方則是另一套配備：短柄銅斧、有脊直刃矛、骨石箭鏃的弓、藤木編的盾，舟船的數量遠超車輛。徐國也有車，但數量與工藝都遜於周王的六師。整場戰役沒有攻城器械的使用記載，糧秣靠車馬與人力沿淮水、汝水兩岸徵發，淮夷的水路運輸反而是他們的優勢。
kitsEn: One thing has to be said first, because it is easy to misread: the Egyptian spear on the card did not march with the Zhou army to Xiashi. It was the typical thrusting weapon of the early Egyptian dynastic period, a copper or bronze head in leaf shape with a central ridge and blade edges on both sides, bound to a wooden shaft with thongs or wooden wedges; the war scene on the reverse of the Narmer palette, the Scorpion Macehead and the carved bone tags showing men hunting elephants all preserve the appearance of men carrying spears, axes and bows. Its functional position is plain: a two-handed thrust at middle range, which could also be thrown in an emergency, used together with a wooden shield faced in hide, complementing the division of labour that later passed to the axe and the adze. Placed in the equipment table of the battle of Xiashi, it corresponds exactly to the ranks of spears in the Zhou line. The Zhou spear was above all a bronze head: leaf-shaped, with a central ridge, blades on either side, and a tubular tang or socket at the back, inserted into a wooden shaft and then bound on with thongs, the shaft itself often wrapped in leather strips or split bamboo, and sometimes finished with a bronze ferrule at the grip. The sets of bronze ge and spears excavated from the early Western Zhou cemetery at Shangcunling in Sanmenxia in Henan and from the Wei state cemetery at Xincun in Jun County in Henan are the material samples of the weapons of this period, and the chariot-and-horse pits at Xincun show how the chariot troops of the day were equipped: two wheels on a single axle, four horses to a car, and three men on the car, one driver, one holding the ge, and one holding a spear or a bow. Alongside the spear stood the ge, whose blade had an upper point and whose socket projected from the haft, and it was fitted to a shaft to be used in hooking, pecking and chopping; it was the other backbone of Zhou infantry and chariot troops. The bow was of bamboo and wood, with arrowheads of stone, of bone and of bronze, and was used to press the enemy before contact and to harry the flanks. Protection was hide armour, leather caps and wooden shields; metal harness was still rare in the Western Zhou. The Huai barbarians carried a different set: short-handled bronze axes, straight-bladed ridged spears, bows with bone and stone arrowheads, and shields of plaited rattan and wood, and they had far more boats than chariots. Xu had chariots too, but in neither number nor workmanship was it the equal of the king's six divisions. There is no record of siege engines at any point in this war: the grain was drawn on the spot by cart and by human porterage along the banks of the Huai and the Ru, and the water transport of the Huai barbarians was their own advantage.
tactics: 這場會戰的經過，只能從零星的編年、詩歌和銘文裡拼回骨架，具體的步驟大致可以這樣復原。第一步是徐方的先手：徐偃王與淮夷聯軍趁周室對淮夷用兵之餘，順淮水而下西進，先取淮西諸邑，再進逼王畿南境與硤石一線；他們熟悉沿淮的渡口、洲渚與沼澤，這是周軍所無的。第二步是周室的集結：宣王調六師自鎬京、成周一帶分道東出，諸侯之師自魯、陳、蔡、杞、宋、衛、晉諸地北來南就，會師之後再沿汝水、淮水南下，前推至硤石；聯軍的糧食大半就地徵發，遠征數百里，時間不能拖太久，這一點決定了後面的速戰速決。第三步是列陣：西周承襲以三軍為主的布陣，中軍居中，左右師分列兩翼，車兵置於中軍與前衛，步兵在車後列為方陣，弓手散在車陣兩側與陣邊；徐軍則倚硤石崗阜與淮水天塹之便，步兵居前拒守，弓手依高處下射，車少而散，淮夷部眾沿水而進，企圖包抄。周軍的打法是先以弓矢在遠程上消耗對方密集的步陣，再以車兵反覆衝擊，把對方陣形扯開，步兵隨車縫壓入，最後由兩翼師截斷徐軍退往淮上的通道。硤石一帶夾在崗地與水患之間，秋季汛期的淮水會抬高水位，道路泥濘，車兵行動受限，這是雙方都受約束的環境條件。第四步是崩潰與追擊：徐軍陣一旦被車兵切斷，退路只剩沿淮向東的狹窄通道，敗兵擁塞於水邊，斬首與生俘的數量因此在官方記錄中特別突出，金文裡「折首」「執訊」這套戰功統計術語正是這樣的戰爭催生的。第五步是收束：詩說「四方既平，徐方來庭」，說明受降與安置被寫進了政治程序；周室隨後把部分淮夷人眾北遷安置，封申伯於謝，築城屯田，作為南面的屏障。
tacticsEn: The course of this meeting of arms can only be reconstructed as a skeleton from scattered annals, a poem and a few inscriptions, and the stages run roughly as follows. The first is Xu's initiative: the army of King Xuan of Xu and the Huai barbarians took advantage of the strain the Zhou campaigns against the Huai had left behind, moved west down the river, took the settlements west of the Huai one by one and then drove in on the southern edge of the royal domain and the line of Xiashi; they knew the fords, the sandbanks and the marshes along the river, and that was something the Zhou did not. The second is the mustering of the Zhou: the king called out the six divisions from Haojing and Chengzhou by separate roads, the contingents of the lords came north from Lu, Chen, Cai, Qi, Song, Wei and Jin to join, and after the meeting the whole force moved south by the Ru and the Huai to press on to Xiashi. The grain of such a coalition was drawn largely on the spot, the distance covered ran to several hundred li, and the campaign could not be prolonged; that fact dictated the speed of the decision. The third is the deployment: the Western Zhou kept the deployment of the three armies, the central host in the middle and the right and the left on the wings, chariot troops placed in the central host and in front, infantry formed up in squares behind the chariots, and archers scattered along the flanks and the edges of the line. The Xu army leaned on the hill country of Xiashi and on the Huai as a natural obstacle, with infantry in front to refuse the attack and archers shooting down from the heights, few chariots and scattered ones, while the Huai groups advanced along the water in the hope of turning the flank. The Zhou method was to wear down the enemy's dense infantry line with arrows at long range, then to strike repeatedly with the chariots to tear the formation open, the infantry pressing in through the gaps the chariots made, and finally for the wings to cut the road by which the Xu army would fall back on the river. The ground at Xiashi was pinched between the hills and the floods: the Huai in high water in the autumn season raises its level, the roads turn to mud, and the movement of the chariots is constrained, a condition that bound both sides. The fourth is the collapse and the pursuit: once the Xu line is cut by the chariots, the only road of retreat left is the narrow bank leading east along the river, the fugitives crowd into the water's edge, and the numbers of those killed and those taken alive are therefore especially prominent in the official record. The technical vocabulary of the bronze inscriptions, the count of the heads cut off and the count of those interrogated, grew out of wars of exactly this kind. The fifth is the closing of the business: the poem says that the four quarters were settled and the Xu came to court, which shows that surrender and resettlement were written into the political programme; the Zhou court then moved part of the Huai population north, enfeoffed the Shen Bo at Xie, and built a city with fields there to serve as a screen on the southern frontier.
data: 可核對的數字分三類，來源可靠程度相差很大。第一類是文獻自述：年份。傳統《竹書紀年》把此役繫在周宣王十一年，按通行西周王年推算落在前817年前後；但近代學者以《詩經·大雅·常武》所記淮夷北遷、申伯封謝，與《左傳》昭公年間徐州之役相校，多主張徐偃王之亂應屬春秋初年，即前515至前514一帶，本卡從前515年；兩個紀年系統相差三百餘年，學界至今沒有定論。戰役月份，傳世文獻沒有明記，通行做法依西周用兵多在秋收之後的慣例推定為秋季，本卡記為九月。軍制規模：師是基本單位，按晚出的制度追述，三軍合七千五百人、六師合一萬五千人，這是編制的量級而不是硤石的實數；戰場上雙方投入多少，沒有任何文獻說得清楚。第二類是金文：兮甲盤（虢季子白盤）銘文記宣王「格伐獫狁于彭衙」，其後又記淮夷來就，王格伐之，銘中有「折首」「執訊」的戰功統計，並記「王錫兮甲馬四匹」及賞車；各家的釋讀在數目上略有出入，所以只能說淮夷之戰的戰果以數十計，俘獲與車馬的量級不為零。師旂鼎則記淮夷所獻的弓與矢。第三類是考古與地理：三門峽上村嶺的西周墓地出土成組青銅戈、矛、削等兵器，浚縣辛村衛國墓地的車馬坑提供西周晚期車乘的樣本；戰場一帶今安徽滁州鳳陽縣西南的硤石山，夾在淮河與其支流之間，去蚌埠數十里，到徐州一線約三四百里；徐國都邑傳在今江蘇泗洪與安徽泗縣之間的徐城，其城址疊壓年代跨度很大，西周層位尚待更多發掘清理。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes of very unequal reliability. The first class is what the texts say of themselves. The date. The received Zhushu Jinian places this campaign in the eleventh year of King Xuan of Zhou, which on the usual reckoning of the Western Zhou regnal years falls around 817 BC; but modern scholars who have compared the northward removal of the Huai people and the enfeoffment of the Shen Bo at Xie recorded in the Shujing's Great Odes chapter Changwu with the wars over Xuzhou in the Zuo Zhuan annals of Duke Zhao have argued for the most part that the rising of King Xuan of Xu belongs to the beginning of the Spring and Autumn period, to the years 515 and 514 BC; this card follows 515 BC. The two chronological systems are more than three hundred years apart and the question is still unsettled. The month: the transmitted texts do not state it, and the usual practice is to infer the autumn from the Zhou habit of taking the field after the harvest, so the card records the ninth month. The scale of the armies: the division was the unit, and the late systematisation of the system gives three armies at seven thousand five hundred men and six divisions at fifteen thousand; that is a scale for the organisation and not a headcount for Xiashi, and no document says how many men either side actually put in the field. The second class is the bronze inscriptions. The pan of Xi Jia, also called the Ji of the Zhai clan, records that the king went to attack the Xianyun at Pengba, and then that the Huaiyi came in and the king attacked them; the inscription carries the battle statistics of the heads cut off and the prisoners interrogated, and records that the king granted Xi Jia four horses and a chariot. Readings differ a little between scholars on the numbers, so the most that can be said is that the results of the war against the Huaiyi ran to tens and that the quantity of prisoners and of captured chariots and horses was not negligible. The ding of Shi Qi records bows and arrows surrendered by the Huaiyi. The third class is archaeology and geography. The early Western Zhou cemetery at Shangcunling in Sanmenxia has yielded sets of bronze ge, spears and knives, and the chariot-and-horse pits at Xincun in Jun County supply the model of the late Western Zhou chariot; the hill of Xiashi to the south-west of Fengyang in Chuzhou, Anhui, where the battle was fought, lies between the Huai and its tributaries, a few tens of li from Bengbu and some three or four hundred li from the line of Xuzhou; the capital of Xu is traditionally placed at the City of Xu between Sihong in Jiangsu and Sixian in Anhui, and the layers of that site span a very long period, with the early Western Zhou horizon still awaiting more excavation.
cause: 打起來的原因可以分四層。最表層是徐國與淮夷的軍事壓力：徐國地處淮水中下游，控住華夏與江淮的通道；淮夷則以舟楫之利沿淮活動，能在短時間內把大量兵力投到任何一個渡口。兩者結盟，等於在周室南翼插上一支可以獨立行動的聯軍，宣王在淮夷方向用兵之後留下的消耗與空隙，正好被徐偃王利用。第二層是周王室重建秩序的需要：西周中期以後，王畿以外諸侯的服從度一直在下降，王室需要一次能拿來號召諸侯的勝利，把「王師討逆」這套話語重新立住；召集來的聯軍名冊本身就是政治展示。第三層是地理與族群結構：徐國與淮夷在文化上同屬東方系統，聯合並不困難；反過來，若徐國倒向淮夷，魯、陳、蔡、杞、宋一帶的諸侯便直接暴露在淮夷的刀鋒之下，這是諸侯肯於出兵的政治理由。第四層是事後的敘事需要：勝方把這場戰爭寫成「徐方騚動」而王「赫赫斯怒」，四方既平而「徐方來庭」，是典型的以詩筆為史筆定調；文獻中沒有留下徐國反叛的原始理由，只留下周室一方對它的指控。這一點很重要：硤石之役的起因，目前只能從勝方的記錄與地理條件反推，而無法從戰敗方自己留下的材料中驗證。
causeEn: The reasons for the war can be set out in four layers. At the surface is the military pressure of Xu together with the Huai barbarians. Xu stood in the middle and lower Huai valley and held the passage between the Central Plain and the river country; the Huai barbarians moved along the river on their boats and could concentrate a large force at any one ford in a short time. An alliance between the two planted in the southern flank of the Zhou court an army that could act on its own, and the strain and the gaps left by the king's own campaigns against the Huai were exactly what King Xuan of Xu used. The second layer is the need of the royal house to restore order. From the middle of the Western Zhou the obedience of the lords beyond the royal domain had been slipping away, and the court needed a victory it could use to summon the lords, to set the language of the royal host punishing rebellion in the market again; the roll of the coalition that answered the call was itself a political demonstration. The third layer is geography and the structure of the peoples. Xu and the Huai groups belonged to the same eastern cultural complex, so joining hands was not difficult; conversely, if Xu went over to the Huai, the lords of Lu, Chen, Cai, Qi and Song would be left directly exposed to the Huai blade, and that is the political reason the lords were willing to bring their troops. The fourth layer is the need of the narrative written afterwards. The winners set the war down as the Xu stirring up trouble and the king swelling with terrible anger, the four quarters settled and the Xu coming to court, which is a typical fixing of the history by the pen of poetry; the documents preserve no original reason for Xu's rising, only the accusation of the Zhou side. That point matters: the cause of the battle of Xiashi can at present only be inferred from the records of the victors and from the geography, and it cannot be verified from any material left by the defeated side itself.
impact: 硤石之役的直接後果是淮南的秩序重排。周室保住了淮北的屏障，徐國沒有被消滅，只是退守淮東、由挑釁的一方變成朝貢的一方；淮夷的部分人眾被北遷安置，申伯受封於謝、築城屯田，華夏王朝的實際控制從此向南推進到淮水兩岸。這個結果也說明西周晚期國力的邊界：聯軍跨越數百里，糧秣就地徵發，遠征的代價不小，而取得的成果不過是一次驅逐。從長時段看，這場戰役是「宣王中興」敘事的支柱，同時也是它的伏線：宣王此後在西陲連敗於戎狄，前線的失敗與南方的成功同時出現，到幽王時犬戎攻入鎬京，兩套問題疊加在一起，終於在西周末年釀成王朝的崩潰。制度層面的影響更為持久：西周國家在此次行動中展示的「王師加諸侯之師」的聯合作戰模式，成為此後數百年諸侯兼併的原型；「淮夷」從此成為王朝文獻中一個固定的政治稱謂，一直沿用到秦漢；徐國的殘餘直到春秋初仍在，楚師在約前512年終於滅徐，徐州之地才真正脫離東方諸國的體系。學術上，這一戰也是復原西周晚期兵制的關鍵節點：它把《竹書紀年》的編年、《大雅·常武》的詩句與兮甲盤、師旂鼎的銘文串成一條線，讓後人知道周室的東南戰線上，車兵、弓兵與被繳獲的淮夷弓矢同時存在。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the battle of Xiashi was a reordering of the order of the country south of the Huai. The Zhou court kept its screen on the north bank of the river; Xu was not destroyed but withdrew to the east of the Huai and changed from the party that had provoked the war into the party that came to court; part of the Huai population was moved north and resettled, the Shen Bo was enfeoffed at Xie with a city and fields built there, and the actual reach of the Central Plain state was pushed south to both banks of the river. The result also shows the limits of Zhou strength in its late phase: a coalition crossing several hundred li, grain taken on the spot, a costly march, and the outcome only a expulsion. Over the long run this battle was a pillar of the narrative of the revival of King Xuan and at the same time a warning shot along the same line: the king afterwards suffered repeated defeats against the Rong and the Di on the western front, failure in the north and success in the south appearing at the same time, and when the Di attacked Haojing in the time of King You, the two sets of problems came together and the dynasty came apart at the end of the Western Zhou. The institutional effect was the more durable of the two. The pattern shown in this campaign, the royal host joined by the contingents of the feudal lords, became the prototype for the wars of annexation that followed for several centuries. The term Huaiyi became from that point a fixed political designation in the dynastic documents and was used on into the Qin and Han. The remnant of Xu survived into the beginning of the Spring and Autumn period, and it was only when the armies of Chu came out against Xu around 512 BC that the country of Xuzhou was finally drawn out of the system of the eastern states. For scholarship, the battle is also a key point for reconstructing the late Western Zhou military system, because it strings together the chronology of the Zhushu Jinian, the verses of the Great Odes chapter Changwu and the inscriptions on the pan of Xi Jia and the ding of Shi Qi into one line, and lets later readers know that chariot troops, archers and Huai bows and arrows taken as spoil all existed at the same time on the Zhou southeastern front.
result: 公元前515年（或傳統所繫的宣王十一年），硤石一線的會戰以周方大勝告終：徐軍的步陣被車兵切斷，聯軍封住往淮上退路，敗兵在崗地與水邊被截住，斬首與生俘的數量在金文裡留下了統計；徐偃王與殘部退保淮東，徐國仍存，但此後不再有能力與周室對抗。戰爭的收尾被寫得很整齊：徐方來庭，遣使朝見請罪，周室接受降附；淮夷之中一部被北遷安置，申伯受封於謝，召伯整頓其田土，築城以為南屏。王師與諸侯之師各還其國，戰役結束。對徐國而言，這是一場慘敗之後的城下之盟：它保住了徐國的存續，代價是從淮北的挑釁者降為王朝的附庸，東方的盟主位置就此失去。對周室而言，這是一場政治收益遠大於軍事收益的勝利——聯軍得以召集、王室的威儀得以恢復、南方的局勢暫時穩定；但它並沒有解決王畿空虛的問題，也沒有補上國力的缺口，前512年楚師出徐州時，東亞的格局已經改觀。而就兵器史而言，硤石留下的線索是：一方是早已成熟的銅矛加木桿加纏束的刺擊兵器，兩千六百年後在淮河兩岸仍在使用；另一方是同樣古老、卻在各自流域獨立成熟的埃及矛制。兩套東西不必互相借用，卻指向同一個軍事技術的共識——長柄銅刺、配合弓與車、護以盾，才是這個年代真正有效的組合。
resultEn: In 515 BC, or in the eleventh year of King Xuan as the older reckoning has it, the meeting of arms on the line of Xiashi ended in a decisive victory for the Zhou. The infantry line of the Xu army was cut by the chariots, the coalition closed the road back to the river, the fugitives were caught between the hills and the water, and the numbers of those killed and taken alive entered the bronze inscriptions as a set of statistics. King Xuan of Xu fell back with the remnant of his forces to the east of the Huai; Xu survived, but from that point it had no strength left to stand against the Zhou court. The closing of the business was written down very tidily: the Xu came to court, sent envoys to apologise, and the Zhou court accepted the submission. Part of the Huai people were moved north and resettled; the Shen Bo was enfeoffed at Xie, Duke Shao straightened out his fields, and a city was built as a screen on the south. The royal host and the contingents of the lords each went home, and the campaign was over. For Xu this was a surrender negotiated after a ruinous defeat: the state kept its existence, and paid for it by ceasing to be the party that had challenged the north bank of the Huai and becoming instead a vassal of the dynasty, its position as leader of the east lost for good. For the Zhou court the victory brought far more political than military profit: the coalition could be summoned, the court's authority was restored, and the situation in the south was for a time stable. It did not solve the emptiness of the royal domain, and it did not fill the gap in the treasury; when the armies of Chu came out against Xuzhou in 512 BC, the order of East Asia had already changed. For the history of arms, what the battle leaves behind is this: on one side a thrusting weapon of bronze head, wooden shaft and binding that had long been mature and was still in use on both banks of the Huai two thousand six hundred years later; on the other the Egyptian spear system, equally old but independently matured in its own river valley. The two need not have borrowed from one another, and they point to a single consensus of military technique: a long bronze thrust, worked together with bow and chariot and covered by shield, was the combination that was actually effective in this age.
